clue.text: Stores coming down proclaim slump

parts.note: to air a view is to proclaim it publicly
a slump in prices is a drop

explanation.surface: A shop owner announces a slump in trade at the stores.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplies released from an aircraft by parachute are delivered this way, so the stores arrive by falling.

clue.text: Like groups of useful properties

parts.note: as means like, in the sense of similar to
sets are groups of things

explanation.surface: A list of things with useful qualities, as in a property portfolio.
explanation.definitionFit: Valuable possessions or advantages are resources one owns, such as land or skills.

clue.text: It's a step-up for the sailor

definitions.text: It's a step-up for the sailor

parts.words: It's a step-up for the sailor
parts.note: reads like a promotion at sea, but describes a short rope rung lashed across a ship's shrouds for climbing the rigging

explanation.walkthrough: 'step-up' suggests promotion; it is literally a rung a sailor climbs.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the small ropes forming the rungs of a ladder up the rigging of a sailing ship.

clue.text: Rig Louise out as a nun …

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Kit out a woman called Louise in a nun's habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a holy order, such as a monk or sister, is called this as a noun.

clue.text: … and put in peril — her trouble is gay Lothario

indicators.note: put in tells us one piece is placed inside another
trouble here means stir up or disturb, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a nun placed in danger by a womanising seducer.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from the nun at 3, who is in danger. 'trouble' shuffles the two words before it, and 'put in' sets the clue's first word inside the result. 'gay' here means carefree, in its older sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Lothario is the seducer in Rowe's play; a carefree womaniser is a man who flirts with many lovers.

clue.text: University invested in antiques, being anxious to learn

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: curios are antiques or collectable oddities

explanation.surface: A college has put its money into antiques, keen to learn about them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being inquisitive means wanting to find things out, a synonym for eager to know.

clue.text: Signal rod

explanation.surface: A rod held up as a signal.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a prompt telling an actor to begin; the other is the stick used to strike balls in billiards or snooker.

clue.text: Quick to take a pawn in attack

indicators.note: in puts the piece for the pawn inside the piece for the attack

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack
P is the chess abbreviation for pawn

explanation.surface: A chess player is quick to capture a pawn during an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast or swift movement is speedy, a synonym for quick.

clue.text: Virginia's bisexual hero in Florida

explanation.surface: Virginia Woolf's gender-changing hero is spotted on holiday in Florida.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia Woolf's novel follows a hero who lives for centuries and changes sex; the same name belongs to a city in central Florida.

clue.text: Browning's wise thrush was a repetitive example

definitions.text: Browning's wise thrush was a repetitive example

parts.words: Browning's wise thrush was a repetitive example
parts.note: Robert Browning's poem Home-Thoughts, from Abroad describes the wise thrush who sings each tune twice over, so the bird is an instance of a repeating singer

explanation.walkthrough: Browning's line is 'That's the wise thrush; he sings each song twice over'.
explanation.definitionFit: A singing bird or a singer is one who performs melodies, as the thrush does.

clue.text: Attendant to sell tea — it's brewed

indicators.note: brewed suggests stirring up a pot, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the word it, with the 's read as 'is', a link

explanation.surface: A cafe worker is told to sell tea once the pot has brewed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' rearranges SELLTEAIT; the 's of it's is just 'is', joining fodder to indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite is a follower or hanger-on, one who attends a more powerful figure.

clue.text: Gateway support

explanation.surface: A gate post holding up a gate.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the monumental gateway of an Egyptian temple; the other is a tall lattice tower carrying power cables.

clue.text: "What! Has this appear'd again tonight?" (Hamlet)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the scan prints a gap after 'this', and the missing word is what Marcellus calls the Ghost in Act 1 of Hamlet

explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has a blank after 'this'; the solver supplies the word Shakespeare wrote there.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcellus refers to the Ghost as an unnamed object or being, the vague word for whatever has appeared.

clue.text: Stresses surround one with many misfortunes

indicators.note: surround tells us one set of letters encloses the others

parts.note: accents are stresses placed on syllables
I is the Roman numeral for one
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number, so many

explanation.surface: Someone plagued by bad luck finds pressures closing in on every side.
explanation.definitionFit: Mishaps and misadventures are unfortunate events that happen unexpectedly.

clue.text: Party changes sides early on, so it's thought

indicators.note: changes sides means left turns to right, and early on places the swap near the start

parts.note: a celebration is a party

explanation.surface: A politician defects from one party early in their career, after much reflection.
explanation.walkthrough: L (left) becomes R (right) near the start of CELEBRATION; 'changes sides' looks like political defection.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerebration is the act of using the brain, thinking or reasoning.

clue.text: Support instrument for Nanki- Poo, say

definitions.text: Support instrument for Nanki- Poo, say

parts.words: Support instrument for Nanki- Poo, say
parts.note: in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado, the prince Nanki-Poo travels in disguise as a lowly backing player in a town band

explanation.walkthrough: Nanki-Poo introduces himself in The Mikado as a wandering minstrel playing a subordinate brass part; 'support' means the junior player beside the principal.
explanation.definitionFit: The lower-ranked slide-brass player in a band backs up the principal, which is Nanki-Poo's disguise.

clue.text: Characters in Munster — i.e. Christian men

indicators.note: characters here are letters, and taking the letters in the words means rearranging them

explanation.surface: Irish Protestants from the province of Munster are described.
explanation.walkthrough: Munster is a province of Ireland. Fletcher Christian led the crew who seized HMS Bounty in 1789.
explanation.definitionFit: Fletcher Christian's followers on the Bounty were rebel sailors who seized the ship.

clue.text: Opening: prime minister comes to the point

parts.note: premier is another title for a prime minister
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: At the start of a speech, the head of government gets to the point.
explanation.definitionFit: A first performance of a play or film is its opening night.

clue.text: For example, 11 of 23

parts.note: the cross-references point at two five-letter answers that use the same letters in different orders, so one is the other shuffled

explanation.walkthrough: The answers at 11 and 23 are anagrams of each other, so 11 is an instance of the letters of 23 being reallocated.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharing out the same letters in a new arrangement is a reallocation of what is already there.

clue.text: Scoffed free, in fact

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a deed is an act or accomplished fact, as in 'in deed and word'
to rid is to free from something

explanation.surface: Someone claims a person was set free, which is mocked as a fact.
explanation.definitionFit: To mock or ridicule is to jeer at someone with contempt.

clue.text: Continuing to be concerned with departure

parts.note: on means about or concerning, as in a book on birds
a going is a leaving, a departure

explanation.surface: Someone stays on, preoccupied with thoughts of leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in progress and not yet ended is still under way.

clue.text: Very hard to keep fish in a pen

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: It's very difficult to keep fish in an enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Like the metal, extremely tough, unyielding and hard.

clue.text: Vehicle to carry gunners needs excellent recoil in suspensions

indicators.note: a vehicle that carries something holds it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a motor is a car, a vehicle
RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners of the British Army

indicators.note: recoil, a gun's backward kick, tells us the letters run backwards

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written here as the letters A and I

explanation.surface: An artillery tractor tows the guns and must cope with recoil in its suspension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recoil' turns AI into IA at the end. A1 (excellent) is read as letters AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Moratoria are temporary halts or postponements, official suspensions of an activity.

clue.text: Keep the part of the potato we remove

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Save the bit of potato that we cut away.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle's keep is its strongest central stronghold, the main fortified building.

clue.text: Time is 11 perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of the cross-referenced answer could be arranged another way

parts.note: the answer at 11 across, a five-letter word for an object

explanation.surface: A clock reads eleven, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges THING, the answer to 11, into the new word; '11' on its surface looks like an hour.
explanation.definitionFit: The hours of darkness are a period of the day, a time.

clue.text: Give directions to US financial statistician

parts.note: E and N, east and north, are compass directions
Charles Dow, American financial journalist and statistician, gave his name to the Dow Jones index

explanation.surface: Someone passes instructions to an American number cruncher on Wall Street.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestow money or property on someone, as in funding a college chair, is to give.

clue.text: Directing principle of conductor with band

parts.note: a guide conducts people, leading the way
a band of colour is a line or stripe

explanation.surface: An orchestra's conductor lays down the rules of direction for the band.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule giving direction for conduct is a general rule of thumb or policy.

clue.text: The chap whom mehitabel always sounded like

indicators.note: sounded like says we want a word pronounced the same as the one given

parts.note: mehitabel the alley cat in Don Marquis's archy and mehitabel had the catchphrase 'toujours gai', always gai, meaning cheerful

explanation.surface: Asks which fellow the cartoon cat mehitabel kept resembling.
explanation.walkthrough: mehitabel's motto 'toujours gai' (always cheerful) gives GAI, read as an English word to sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow or man is a common informal word for a chap.

clue.text: See about backward Russian scholar, not so young

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the see's letters surround the rest

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, the seat of a bishop and so a see

indicators.note: backward says the following pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: red is old shorthand for a Russian communist
L, a learner, is a student or scholar

explanation.surface: Look at an old-fashioned Soviet academic who is getting on in years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns the Russian and scholar pieces round, and 'about' wraps the see around them. Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone getting on in years is old, the opposite of youthful.

clue.text: Flowers to make the opposition sound happy

indicators.note: sound here means as heard, so the word is replaced by one that is pronounced the same

parts.note: in a parliamentary vote, the noes are those voting against, the opposition
gay in its older sense means cheerful or happy

explanation.surface: A bouquet meant to cheer up one's political rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: The noes are those voting against in Parliament; 'sound' gives a word said the same as theirs, the face's organ of smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bunch of scented blooms, a posy, is a bouquet of flowers.
